2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the materials on record.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with G.R. Case No.980 of 2023, arising out of Khallikote P.S. Case No.384 of 2023, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Khallikote, for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 376/342/506/420/406 of the I.P.C.
4. Pursuant to the notice issued vide order dated 05.09.2024, the victim appeared before this Court by virtual mode by remaining present in the local police station.
The victim stated before this Court that she does not want to proceed further in the matter as the matter has been amicably settled and she has received back her belongings.

On a specific query put by this Court to the victim with regard to voluntariness of her statement, the victim stated that giving such statement on her own volition Harakishor Swain @ Hara @ vs State Of Odisha .....

and free will and she is under no pressure, threat or coercion.
5. Learned counsel for the Petitioner, on the other hand, contended that the Petitioner is in languishing in custody since 05.07.2024.
He further contended that due to misunderstanding, the case has been registered against the Petitioner at the instance of the Informant.
However, the Informant does not want to proceed further in the matter.

6. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that merely because the victim does not want to proceed in the matter, the Petitioner is not entitled to release on bail.

He further submitted that although charge sheet has been filed in the meantime, however, in the event the Petitioner is released on bail, there is every likelihood that he might influence the prosecution witnesses.

7. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and keeping in view the statement of the victim before this Court, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.
8.

Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.35,000/- (Rupees thirty five thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter.

While imposing conditions, the Court in seisin over the matter shall impose conditions whereby the Petitioner shall appear before the trial court on each and every date of posting of the case; and he shall not harass/threaten/terrorize the victim and her family members or any of the prosecution witnesses in any manner whatsoever while on bail.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions imposed by this Court or the Court in seisin over the matter shall entail cancellation of bail.
9. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
